name: USS Grunion

sources.title: USS Grunion — Gato-class submarine lost off Kiska in July 1942; found by the Abele family's search (2006-2007), confirmed by the Navy in 2008
ScienceDaily (2008) — the Navy confirms the wreck is Grunion: about 3,200 ft, cold water and little current keeping much of her intact
Marine Link — submarine confirmed: markings, propeller guards and limber holes matching her design; the hull collapsed

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q6147254_uss_grunion.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/dresskit.py) with AI assistance. At about 1,000 m on the slope off Kiska, settled with a list: the pressure hull partly collapsed (dished in), the casing with its limber holes, the conning-tower fairwater with the periscope shears, the deck gun, the planes and the two screws with their guards; the bow broken off and lying a little apart, at the end of the furrow she cut in the slope. A war grave (70 men). The break, the furrow and the heading (not published: 0) are approximate. model_built.glb: the submarine as commissioned in 1942. No marine life in the model: Offlined draws the living things itself.
